questions.title: Rescue Boats Two Per Raft
questions.description:
A rescue crew evacuates people with rafts that carry at most TWO people whose weights sum to at most limit: sort the weights, then greedily pair the lightest remaining person with the heaviest remaining one when they fit together, otherwise send the heaviest alone; return the number of rafts. Sort-based sweep — priority_queue is banned. Input format: line 1 has n; line 2 has n integers. The harness collects them in a vector<int>, in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int num_boats(std::vector<int> people, int limit)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n weights. Line 3: limit.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of rafts.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= weight <= limit <= 1000

questions.title: Content Children Count
questions.description:
A snack drive matches cookies to children: child i is content with a cookie of size >= greed[i], and each cookie feeds at most one child. Sort both lists, then sweep the smallest cookies against the smallest unmet greeds and return how many children become content. Sort-based sweep — unordered_ containers are banned. Input format: line 1 has n and line 2 has n greed values; line 3 has m and line 4 has m cookie sizes. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int content_children(std::vector<int> greed, std::vector<int> cookies)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n greed values. Line 3: m. Line 4: m cookie sizes.

Output Format:
One line with the number of content children.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 50, 1 <= greed, cookie size <= 1000

Input format: line 1 has n; each of the next n lines has two integers a and b, one pair per line. The harness collects them in the vector<pair<int,int>> (a = first, b = second), in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Next n lines: start finish.

Output Format:
One line with the 0-based index of the earliest-finishing activity.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= start < finish <= 100000

questions.title: One Boat or Two
questions.description:
A rescue crew checks a raft pairing: each raft carries at most two people whose weights sum to at most the limit. Given two weights w1 and w2, return 1 when they can share one raft (w1 + w2 <= limit), else 2 when each needs their own raft.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int boats_for_two(int w1, int w2, int limit)

Input Format:
One line: w1 w2 limit.

Output Format:
One line: 1 if they can share a raft, else 2.

Constraints:
1 <= w1, w2 <= limit <= 100000

questions.title: Largest Cookie for the Child
questions.description:
A snack table serves one child: return the LARGEST cookie size that does not exceed the child's greed (a cookie of size >= greed satisfies the child, but we hand the biggest one that still fits the rule size <= greed), or -1 when no cookie is small enough. Input format: line 1 has m; line 2 has m cookie sizes; line 3 has the child's greed g. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

    int best_cookie(const std::vector<int>& cookies, int greed)

Input Format:
Line 1: m. Line 2: m cookie sizes. Line 3: greed.

Output Format:

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 50, 1 <= cookie size, greed <= 100000

questions.title: Pack the Van in Order
questions.description:
A loader packs boxes strictly in delivery order and never reorders: walk the weights in input order, loading each box while it fits in the remaining capacity; stop at the FIRST box that does not fit and return how many boxes were loaded. Input format: line 1 has n; line 2 has n integers. The harness collects them in a vector<int>, in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Line 1: n. Line 2: n weights. Line 3: capacity.

Output Format:
One line with the number of boxes loaded.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= weight, capacity <= 100000

questions.title: Two Trains, One Platform
questions.description:
A tiny station checks a timetable pair: a train occupies its platform from arrival up to (not including) departure, so two trains clash exactly when a1 < d2 AND a2 < d1. Return 2 when the trains clash (two platforms needed), else 1.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

    int platforms_for_two(int a1, int d1, int a2, int d2)

Input Format:
One line: a1 d1 a2 d2.

Output Format:
One line: 2 if the trains overlap, else 1.

Constraints:
0 <= arrival < departure <= 100000

1 <= n <= 50, bills are 5, 10 or 20

Sort-based sweep — priority_queue is banned. Input format: line 1 has n; the next n lines each have duration and deadline. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= length <= 100000

questions.title: Fractional Loot Value
questions.description:
A treasure vault holds loot items, each with a weight and a value; the sack has a weight capacity, and items may be TAKEN FRACTIONALLY (taking a fraction f of an item yields fraction f of its value). Maximize the sack's total value: repeatedly pick the remaining item with the best value-per-weight ratio, take it whole when it fits or the fitting fraction when it does not, and stop at full capacity. The reference scans for the best remaining ratio each step — sort( is banned, track picks in a taken array. Input format: line 1 has n; the next n lines each have weight and value; the last line has the capacity. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Output Format:

Input format: line 1 has n; the next n lines each have deadline and profit. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

    long long job_profit(std::vector<std::pair<int,int>> jobs)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Next n lines: deadline profit.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum total profit.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= deadline <= 100, 1 <= profit <= 100000
